summary: The six spectra fall into three groups by mode position and width, not by thickness. B, D and F have sharp modes with the ~110 cm-1 mode at 112-114 cm-1 (FWHM 4.2-4.8 cm-1). C and E have soft, broad modes (~104 and ~238 cm-1, FWHM 8.7-9.5 cm-1) and a weak hump near 302 cm-1. A is intermediate and very strong. Thickness cannot be assigned from these six spectra alone. The only thickness-sensitive channel for layered vdW materials (interlayer shear/breathing modes, below ~50 cm-1) is outside the measured window. A tentative ranking by the strength of the 341 cm-1 mode relative to the local background is D > F > A > B > E > C, but this is a signal-strength proxy and is confounded by orientation, substrate contrast, focus and background. Treat it as low confidence until AFM is in hand.

observations.finding: Two spectral families: B, D, F have sharp modes; C and E have soft, broad modes and a ~302 cm-1 hump; A is intermediate
The 341 cm-1 (P4) mode is the strongest feature in all six flakes; its centre spreads by ~2.7 cm-1 and its width ranges 4.2-7.1 cm-1
Signal strength relative to local background ranks D > F > A > B > E > C; this is the only quantity that ordering rests on
observations.evidence: P4 height / background at centre: D 5.52, F 4.24, A 3.58, B 2.46, E 1.51, C 0.86. Background = mean counts 150-230 cm-1: A 3075, F 3500, D 1746, E 1689, C 1061, B 931. Background is high where the peaks are strongest (A, F), so collection efficiency likely scales everything together.

observations.finding: Mode-area ratios differ between flakes and do not follow the signal ranking, so they probably reflect orientation or local environment rather than thickness
observations.evidence: Area ratios from fits. P2/P4: B 0.478, F 0.490, D 0.279, C 0.131, E 0.121, A 0.073. P1/P4: B 0.398, D 0.379, F 0.337, A 0.251, C 0.121, E 0.119. The 0.07 for A's P2/P4 is the largest outlier.

observations.finding: The ~302 cm-1 feature is only a real peak in C and E; in A it is marginal and in B, D and F the fitted amplitude is zero or negative
observations.evidence: P3 fitted peak height above background: C 243 counts (centre 302.3), E 724 counts (302.1), A 429 counts (301.4, sits on a rising background), B/D/F no peak (fit amplitude <=0 or unstable). Fit plots show no peak in B, D, F.

observations.finding: The P1 and P2 shifts in C and E are larger than the P4 shift and are not a global calibration offset
observations.evidence: P4-P2 spacing (cm-1): A 99.64, B 98.45, C 102.56, D 98.13, E 101.41, F 97.85. The spacing changes by 4.7 cm-1 across flakes, so the shifts are mode-specific, not a uniform axis offset. Centre errors on C P1 (0.33) and E P1 (0.20) are larger but the ~8 cm-1 shift is well outside them.

observations.finding: Peak position does not track signal strength: the sharpest flake (B) is weak and the strongest flake (F) is not the most blue-shifted
observations.evidence: P1 centre vs P4 height: C 103.8/1125, E 103.7/3406, A 108.6/12721, D 113.3/9769, F 111.9/17065, B 114.0/2226. The relationship is not monotonic.

observations.finding: Data grid and quality: no NaNs; 313 points from 50.75 to 430.84 cm-1; step varies 1.18-1.26 cm-1; the lower edge (50-80 cm-1) is dominated by the Rayleigh filter edge
observations.evidence: Mean step 1.2182 cm-1, min 1.1811, max 1.2573. Intensity floor ~680 counts identical across all six at 50-70 cm-1. Rise between ~70 and ~85 cm-1 is the filter edge.

observations.finding: Thickness-sensitive low-frequency interlayer modes are not in the measured window
observations.evidence: Spectra start at 50.75 cm-1 and the filter edge rises through ~70-85 cm-1, so modes below ~50 cm-1 cannot be measured in these files.

caveats: Ranking by 341 cm-1 signal strength is a proxy. The same intensity can come from different thickness, in-plane orientation (CrSBr is strongly anisotropic), substrate optical contrast (SiO2 thickness), focus, or a different collection efficiency. The background (150-230 cm-1 counts: 931-3500) is large and varies between flakes, and the peak-to-background ratio is only partly corrected for it.

At 532 nm, bulk-like absorption limits the probed depth. Above a certain thickness the signal saturates, so the strongest flakes may all be thick and the ranking cannot separate them. The penetration depth is an order-of-magnitude estimate I did not verify.

C and E have soft, broad modes and a ~302 cm-1 hump. Possible causes: thin flakes with weak signal, strain, defects, local heating, or a different orientation. Local heating would need a temperature coefficient of about 0.01-0.02 cm-1/K (an assumed typical range, not checked for CrSBr) to produce a ~5 cm-1 shift, which implies hundreds of K at 200 uW and seems unlikely, but a power series would settle it.
The 302 cm-1 hump could be a real mode, a PL/background feature or a fit artefact. Its amplitude is only 243-724 counts above background, so it is weak.

Fit uncertainties are statistical (0.01-0.05 cm-1 for P4). The real uncertainty is larger because the spectra are sampled at 1.2 cm-1 and the calibration is not checked against a Si reference. Widths should be read as +/-0.3 cm-1 at best.
Mode ratios (P1/P4, P2/P4) are orientation-dependent in anisotropic materials, so they should not be read as thickness indicators without polarization data.
questions_for_user: Substrate type and SiO2 thickness (or other oxide) for the marked substrate? Optical contrast changes the Raman intensity strongly and non-monotonically with thickness.
Was a Si reference peak (520.7 cm-1) measured in the same session? The P2-P4 spacing varies by 4.7 cm-1 across flakes, so I cannot rule out per-flake axis drift without it.

Was the linear polarization or analyzer orientation controlled, and was each flake measured at the same in-plane angle? If not, intensity and mode-ratio differences may reflect orientation rather than thickness.

Can you extend the acquisition below ~70 cm-1 with a low-frequency (ultra-low-frequency) configuration? Interlayer shear and breathing modes are the most direct thickness marker in layered materials, and they are absent here.
Is the broad background PL or fluorescence? A wider spectral window (for example 100-1000 cm-1 plus a PL scan) would separate PL from substrate background.
What objective, spot size and exposure were used, and was each flake measured at a single spot? Spot-to-spot variation within a flake has not been assessed.
Were the spectra exported raw or resampled? The step varies from 1.18 to 1.26 cm-1, which is more than I would expect from a linear pixel-to-wavenumber axis.
Would you like a power series on one soft flake (C or E) and one sharp flake (B or D) to test heating directly? Stokes/anti-Stokes ratios would give the local temperature.
Please share AFM thickness for the six flakes when available. I would rerank and recalibrate the signal-strength proxy against it.
